title: Asking for a break when I need one
examples: How do I ask for a break?
What if I need a break in class?

explain.say: Look at the board. Sometimes a feeling keeps growing inside you. On the left is holding it in. On the right is asking for a break. Asking for a break is a good choice.

draw.text: Asking for a break when I need one

explain.say: The left side is holding it in. The feeling can get bigger. Your grown-up does not know you need help. It is hard to learn. Have you felt like that?
The right side is asking for a break. Your grown-up can help you. You get a short, calm break. Then you come back, ready to learn. Which side feels better?
Here are the steps. First, notice your body feels too full or too busy. Then ask. You can say, Can I have a break, please? Take a few calm minutes. Then come back. Can you say the words with me?

explain.say: There are many ways to ask. You can use words, like I need a minute. You can show a break card or a hand signal. You can point to a picture. Today, choose your way to ask with your teacher.

faq.q: What words can I use to ask for a break?
faq.a: You can say, Can I have a break, please? or I need a minute, please. Short and calm is perfect.

faq.q: How do I know I need a break?
faq.a: Check your body. Hot face, tight fists, wiggly legs or a full head are signs. Ask early, before the feeling gets too big.

faq.q: What if my teacher says not now?
faq.a: Your teacher might say, In two minutes. Take a slow breath and wait. If it is very hard, you can say, I really need it, please. A grown-up you trust can help you make a plan.
It is a small card you can show your teacher when talking feels hard. It means, I need a break, please.

faq.q: Why is holding feelings in hard?
faq.a: Feelings can grow when nobody knows about them. A short break helps them settle.

facts: Many schools use break cards so children can ask for a break without words.
A short break can help people return to work feeling calmer.
